claims.claim_text: Affirm relies on Celtic Bank to originate substantially all loans facilitated through its platform.
claims.source_quote: We currently rely on Celtic Bank to originate substantially all of the loans facilitated through our platform. If our agreement with Celtic Bank is terminated, and we are unable to replace their commitments, our business, results of operations, financial condition, and future prospects would be materially and adversely affected.
claims.subject: Celtic Bank
claims.extraction_notes: Celtic Bank is FDIC-insured Utah state-chartered industrial bank. If AFRM's claim is true, Celtic's Call Report LNCONOTH (other consumer loans) should be very large and roughly track AFRM's GMV cadence over recent quarters. Scorer should also verify FDIC charter via fdic_bankfind.query_institution.

claims.claim_text: Cross River Bank, an FDIC-insured New Jersey state-chartered bank, is one of Affirm's originating bank partners and also provides the FDIC-insured high-yield savings account through the Affirm app.
claims.source_quote: A portion of these loans are funded and issued by our originating bank partners, which include Cross River Bank, an FDIC-insured New Jersey state-chartered bank, and Celtic Bank, an FDIC-insured Utah state-chartered industrial bank. ... High-yield savings account. Through the Affirm app and in partnership with Cross River Bank, we offer an FDIC-insured, interest-bearing savings account, with no minimum deposit requirements or fees.
claims.subject: Cross River Bank
claims.extraction_notes: Verify FDIC charter, NJ state-chartered, and active status. Scorer may chain with fdic_call_reports.query_bank_credit_history for portfolio sizing. AFRM's specific share within Cross River's overall consumer-loan book is not separable; this is partner-existence + charter adjudication, not share.

claims.claim_text: Affirm entered into a commercial agreement with Amazon (Amazon.com Services LLC) on November 10, 2021, granting Amazon warrants to purchase 22,000,000 shares of Affirm Class A common stock, and Amazon-related warrant expense was a material driver of FY2023 commercial agreement expense ($182.3M increase).
claims.source_quote: During the year ended June 30, 2022, we granted warrants to purchase 22,000,000 shares of common stock in connection with our commercial agreements with Amazon. 7,000,000 of the warrant shares have an exercise price of $0.01 per share and a term of 3.5 years, while the remaining 15,000,000 warrant shares have an exercise price of $100 per share and a term of 7.5 years. ... commercial agreement expense, which increased by $167.3 million primarily as a result of an increase of $182.3 million related to Amazon warrant expenses
claims.subject: Amazon.com Services LLC
claims.extraction_notes: Layer 3 Rule 7: material BNPL merchant relationship should appear in Amazon's filings. Counterparty corroboration of Amazon as AFRM merchant partner. Single-word 'Affirm' restricted to AMZN CIK should return hits if disclosed.

claims.source_quote: 10.6 Customer Installment Program Agreement, dated as of July 16, 2020, by and between Shopify Inc. and Affirm, Inc. ... 10.12 Amendment No. 5 to Customer Installment Program Agreement, dated March 31, 2023 by and between Shopify, Inc. and Affirm, Inc.

claims.claim_text: Affirm sponsors asset-backed securitization trusts that issue notes to third-party investors (notes issued by securitization trusts $2.17 billion outstanding as of June 30, 2023), indicating ongoing programmatic ABS issuance.
claims.source_quote: Securities issued from our asset-backed securitizations are senior or subordinated, based on the waterfall criteria of loan payments to each security class. ... Notes issued by securitization trusts 2,165,577 ... Our durable funding model consists of three primary channels warehouse credit facilities, programmatic issuance of term and revolving securitization transactions, and forward flow commitments.
claims.subject: Affirm Holdings
claims.extraction_notes: Categorized as financial_distress for the cohort taxonomy (capital-markets-access proxy). ABS-15G / 10-D filing cadence directly adjudicates programmatic-securitization claim. Note: AFRM uses dedicated SPE issuers (e.g. Affirm Asset Securitization Trust) which may file under different CIKs; scorer may need to also search by issuer name.

claims.claim_text: As of June 30, 2023, Affirm had approximately 254,000 active merchants and approximately 36 million consumers who have transacted on the platform, with $20.2 billion in fiscal 2023 GMV facilitated.
claims.source_quote: As of June 30, 2023, we had approximately 254,000 active merchants ... As of June 30, 2023, almost 36 million consumers have trusted Affirm as their transaction partner. ... We have already achieved significant scale, facilitating consumer purchases of $20.2 billion in GMV in fiscal year 2023.
claims.subject: Affirm
claims.extraction_notes: Calibration Heuristic 3: GMV is gross merchandise volume facilitated, NOT Affirm revenue. Active-merchant and active-consumer counts are internal management metrics with no authoritative external registry analog. Genuinely UNVERIFIABLE structurally for the framework; included to anchor scale context, not for adjudication.

claims.claim_text: Affirm operates internationally in Canada through subsidiary PayBright and maintains Canadian-loan warehouse credit facilities aggregating $548.4 million of revolving commitment as of June 30, 2023 (of which $349.6 million drawn).
claims.source_quote: We use various credit facilities to finance the origination of loan receivables in Canada. ... As of June 30, 2023, the aggregate commitment amount of these facilities was $548.4 million on a revolving basis, of which $349.6 million was drawn. ... a gain of $8.2 million recognized based on a change in the fair value of the contingent consideration liability associated with our acquisition of PayBright
claims.subject: Affirm (Canada via PayBright)

proposed_connector.name: osfi_canada.query_lender_credit_facilities
proposed_connector.description: OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions Canada) plus SEDAR+ filings registry for Canadian-domiciled lender subsidiaries and their disclosed funding arrangements.
proposed_connector.sample_invocation: GET https://www.sedarplus.ca/csa-party/records/document.html?id=<PayBright filing> OR scrape SEDAR+ for filings by 'PayBright' / 'Affirm Canada Holdings ULC'
proposed_connector.rationale: AFRM's Canadian lending stack runs through PayBright as a non-bank lender; OSFI doesn't directly regulate non-bank consumer-installment lenders, but SEDAR+ is the canonical Canadian filings registry that would show any public-debt issuance, syndicate disclosures, or Canadian subsidiary returns. No US registry adjudicates Canadian non-bank lender warehouse capacity.
proposed_connector.completeness: Canadian reporting issuers and certain regulated entities only; private warehouse facilities to non-reporting subsidiaries often invisible.

claims.extraction_notes: Hard claim to adjudicate: PayBright is a private Canadian subsidiary, warehouse facilities are bilateral and not publicly registered. The proposed connector is a best-effort path; realistically this claim may remain UNVERIFIABLE. Included to surface the gap — Canadian non-bank lender funding has no US/Canadian authoritative registry.
